sidecar.title: Head and flow: how much power is in your stream?
sidecar.description: An original animated explainer. Hydro power comes from two numbers, head and flow. P = rho x g x Q x H x efficiency, a worked example for a small UK hill stream (5 L/s and 10 m head gives about 245 W), how to measure flow with a bucket and head with a water-filled hose, and a rule of thumb you can do in your head.

sidecar.title: Watts vs watt-hours: power, energy and your daily budget
sidecar.description: An original animated explainer. Watts are power, a rate; watt-hours are energy, power times time. Why a small stream's 245 W all day (5,880 Wh) beats a 400 W solar panel's three sunny hours (1,200 Wh), how to list your loads in watt-hours a day (a Starlink dish, a laptop, LED lights and phone charging come to about 2,820 Wh), where the spare goes, and the rule that a hydro generator never runs without a load: it needs a dump (diversion) load, or it overspeeds and the voltage spikes.

sidecar.title: Volts, amps and ohms
sidecar.description: An original animated explainer. Volts are the push, amps are the flow and ohms are the resistance, pictured as head, flow and a narrow pipe. Ohm's law (volts = amps × ohms), power = volts × amps, and why the stream's 245 W is about 20 A at 12 V but only about 5 A at 48 V: a quarter of the current, and a sixteenth of the heat lost in the same cable. Plus why low voltage is not the same as safe, and the rule that a hydro generator never runs without a load.

sidecar.title: The fire triangle
sidecar.description: An original animated explainer. Dry firewood holds about 4 kWh of heat per kilogram, and fire is how we let it out. A fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen: take away any one and it goes out. Building a fire from tinder up through spaghetti-thin, finger-thick and wrist-thick sticks, why dry wood matters (Ready to Burn: 20% moisture or less), how a fire steel makes sparks, and the safety rules: never a fire or barbecue in a tent, the Countryside Code, and drown, stir, drown again, check it's cold.
